# ADR 0003: Progressive quick and detailed estimates

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

## Status

Superseded by ADR 0004. This record preserves the intermediate design and is not the
current product or scientific contract.

## Context

A complete 2,048-register chromosome overview is more accurate than a small sketch,
but scientific refinement must not delay the first interactive plot. Occasional
window loss near the low-identity boundary is acceptable estimator variance; the
interactive application does not require a zero-miss guarantee.

## Decision

Every sketch level is rendered in two immutable quality passes:

* a 256-register quick estimate is displayed first;
* a configurable detailed estimate, defaulting to 2,048 registers, replaces each
  quick tile in the background;
* quick axis sketches are constructed at the quick register count without retaining
  sparse exact-correction sets; they are not prefixes of an eagerly constructed
  detailed sketch;
* detailed construction begins only after the renderer acknowledges a painted quick
  frame;
* navigation assigns a new request generation, drops queued work for the previous
  viewport, and retains only already completed parameter-keyed tiles;
* visible quick tiles precede halo quick tiles, which precede detailed work;
* exact k-mer tiles remain the terminal zoom level and do not use sketch refinement.

The bounded sparse correction is part of detailed tiles only. At 80% ANI, the
estimator computes the expected true OPH match count from the directed core/target
cardinalities. Correction is eligible when

```text
P(at least one true match) = 1 - exp(-expected_matches) < 0.99
```

This is equivalent to fewer than 4.605 expected matches under the Poisson model. A
complete exact core is retained only through 2,048 distinct canonical hashes; larger
cores remain approximate. The condition controls the probability of complete window
loss, not the numerical precision of a one-match containment estimate.

Quick and detailed register counts are advanced options. A future image or numeric
export defaults to the detailed count associated with its view and may request a
custom register count and output size. Export is not implemented in this milestone.

## Consequences

First paint is governed by the quick pass rather than final matrix completion. The
same viewport can visibly sharpen without changing coordinates, score definition,
or color settings. Detailed work is opportunistic and cancellable between tile jobs.
The cache is byte-budgeted and uses recency rather than entry count because register
tiers have materially different memory costs. The exact channel is smaller and
probabilistic by design, so validation reports must
describe miss distributions rather than claiming a universal window guarantee.
